Context/Background:
Sonic hedgehog medulloblastoma (SHH-MB), characterized by hyperactivation of the namesake SHH signaling pathway, accounts for ∼30% of all MBs and occurs across all age groups. Cerebellar granule neuron progenitors (GNPs) are the developmental origin of SHH-MB. Germline loss-of-function (LOF) variants in Elongator acetyltransferase complex subunit 1 (ELP1) are the most prevalent predisposing genetic events in childhood medulloblastoma (MB), accounting for ∼30% of the Sonic hedgehog (SHH) 3 subtype. The mechanism(s) by which germline ELP1 deficiency provokes SHH-MB pathogenesis remain unknown. To resolve the mechanistic basis of ELP1-associated SHH-MB, we generated a germline Elp1+/− mouse model using CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing (designated as Elp1HET mice).

To evaluate the tumorigenic potential of germline Elp1 deficiency using an orthotopic transplantation model, GNPs were isolated from Cas9-GFP;Elp1HET and Cas9-GFP;Elp1WT littermates, transduced with gRNA-carrying lentivirus targeting the SHH-3 MB driver Ptch1, and implanted into the cerebella of immunocompromised mice.
Prompt: Provide a cohesive explanation of positively and negatively enriched pathways based on differential genes of Elp1HET;Ptch1gRNA vs Elp1WT;Ptch1gRNA tumors.

Introduction/Context  
Sonic-hedgehog medulloblastoma (SHH-MB) arises from cerebellar granule neuron progenitors (GNPs) and is driven in part by Ptch1 LOF. Germline heterozygous loss of Elp1 (Elp1HET) predisposes to SHH-MB but the mechanism is unknown. To model this, GNPs from Cas9-GFP;Elp1HET vs Cas9-GFP;Elp1WT mice were transduced with Ptch1-targeting gRNA, orthotopically transplanted, and subjected to RNA-seq–based preranked GSEA (Elp1HET;Ptch1gRNA vs Elp1WT;Ptch1gRNA). Lead enriched terms span vesicle trafficking/synaptic biology vs ribosome and RNA processing.  

Keywords  
• Synaptic vesicle exocytosis  
• rRNA/ribosome biogenesis  
• Elp1 (Elongator complex)  
• Ptch1 (SHH-3 driver)  
• Pre-mRNA processing

Analysis  
Elp1 heterozygosity markedly upregulates synaptic- and vesicle-related compartments and processes (GOCC, GOBP, Reactome), with nearly 90% of GOCC terms and ~50% of GOBP terms positively enriched. Core exocytic machinery genes (Snap25, Rab3a, Syt1) and neurotransmitter transport/secretion modules are dominant, suggesting enhanced secretory/synaptic dynamics in Elp1HET tumors. Conversely, ribosome biogenesis, rRNA metabolism, ncRNA processing, DNA replication, and cell-cycle regulators are downregulated (GOBP, Reactome), indicating a shift from proliferation and core RNA-processing to specialized secretory functions. The ratio inversion in GOBP/Reactome (more down than up) underscores coordinated repression of biosynthetic pathways alongside synaptic-vesicle activation. This dual axis—secretory boost vs translational/replication damping—may reflect Elp1’s role in neuronal lineage maintenance and how its LOF reprograms growth vs differentiation cues in SHH-MB.
